Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.

meanings.note: Surprise, fright or pain. Core Russian interj meaning 'oh' in everyday speech.
Enclose completely on all sides. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to surround, to encircle', paired with 'окружать'.

examples.trans: Comrade commander, the building is completely surrounded.

meanings.note: Done in response to an action. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('return, retaliatory, responsive').

examples.text: Наша команда быстро забила ответный гол.
examples.trans: Our team quickly scored a return goal.

meanings.note: a door, window, bottle, or business

examples.trans: I'm going to open it now.
They open the shop at nine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Colloquial figuratively. Common masculine noun meaning 'partisan, guerrilla' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: Inflict a physical wound. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wound, to injure', paired with 'ранить'.

examples.trans: You are wounded in the arm.

examples.text: Она чуть не ранила меня этим ножом!
examples.trans: She almost injured me with this knife!

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.
Also a Russian man (as a noun). Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Russian').

examples.trans: Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give up, to surrender', paired with 'сдаться'.

examples.text: Никогда не сдавайся! Сегодня я выйду отсюда под подписку!
examples.trans: Never give up! Today I'm getting out of here on a travel ban!

meanings.note: Capitulate to an opponent. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to surrender, to give up', paired with 'сдаваться'.

examples.trans: Raise your hands and surrender to the authorities.

examples.text: Тогда я, пожалуй, сдамся прямо сразу.
examples.trans: Then I think I will surrender right away.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives

Я считаю, что... = I think that. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'читать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.
